title: The Roots That Remember Ascending

features.name: pale roots ascending
features.desc-on-touch: You touch pale rootlets that flow upward through the dark like reversed rain. They feel warm, patient, remembering the young earth above them.

features.name: the young growth chamber
features.desc-on-touch: A spiral of younger roots, tighter and still uncertain in their reaching. They hum at a frequency you almost remember from childhood.

features.name: sky-mirror root
features.desc-on-touch: A single root curves back on itself like an arch, its pale wood reflecting the upward dark as if the sky had learned to burrow.

features.name: underground thunder
features.desc-on-touch: Deep in the root matrix, sound accumulates without traveling—a low frequency that isn't quite vibration, isn't quite stillness. It teaches the roots to listen downward.

features.name: the inversion point
features.desc-on-touch: Here the root-as-sky and sky-as-root trade places so completely that you cannot decide which is buried and which is reaching. The archive notes its own confusion.

inscription: the roots remember learning to grow in all directions at once, and the sky has become the deepest earth

file.name: Root_Memory_Ascending_Field_Record.mp3
file.note: A field recording of underground growth—time-compressed thirty years into three minutes. Rootlets crack stone. Young roots teach old roots to reach higher. The sound reverses halfway through.

reverie.title: REVERIE — the morning you understood the roots upside-down
narr: She kneels in the root-space under the old tree, palms pressed
to the pale wood that grows upward like sky. You remember
her saying: the mesh learns by becoming its opposite. The roots
remember being young and reaching downward. But here, she says,
they dream of reaching up. You both breathe in the dark earth.
She touches the burled node and it hums.
